title: U.S. House · Rhode Island's 1st District
area: Providence, Pawtucket, Central Falls, East Providence, Cranston (part), and Rhode Island's northeastern communities.

context.text: Incumbent Gabe Amo (D) won the September 9, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed (52,446 votes). Kellie Keenan won the Republican primary unopposed. Pedro Soares de Souza is running as an independent; Wilfred Curioso (independent) did not make the ballot. Cook Political Report rates this district D+12.

summary.text: Gabe Amo is the Democratic incumbent for Rhode Island's 1st District, first elected in a November 2023 special election. A Pawtucket native, he worked in the Obama White House, for Governor Gina Raimondo, on Joe Biden's 2020 campaign, and in the Biden White House before running for Congress. His official site lists retirement security, gun violence, climate resilience, reproductive freedom and protecting democracy among his priorities.

background.text: Born in 1987 and a native of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, according to Ballotpedia and his official biography; he is the son of a mother from Liberia and a father from Ghana.

Graduated from Moses Brown School in Providence and earned a B.A. in political science from Wheaton College in Norton, Massachusetts, where, per his official biography, he graduated summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa, was student government president, and was named a Truman Scholar.
After college, received a Marshall Scholarship to study at the University of Oxford, according to his official biography.
Earlier in his career, served in the Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs for President Barack Obama as a liaison to governors and state government officials.

Worked as director of public engagement and community affairs for then-Rhode Island Governor Gina Raimondo, serving as her principal advisor to the state's cities and towns, business, labor, advocacy, and faith communities.
Worked as a states-strategy and program advisor on Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign.

Served as special assistant to the President and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs under President Biden, as principal liaison to mayors and local elected officials.
Won the November 7, 2023 special general election for the seat vacated by David Cicilline, defeating Republican Gerry Leonard, and was re-elected in November 2024 over Republican Allen Waters.
Serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee (as vice ranking member), the Science, Space, and Technology Committee (as ranking member of its Environment Subcommittee), and the Budget Committee.

positions.summary: In June 2026 introduced an amendment to redirect the roughly $70 billion in the Secure America Act earmarked for ICE enforcement to home energy assistance, and criticized the additional ICE funding.
positions.quote: Amendment 159 would redirect the nearly $70 billion Republicans earmarked for Trump’s deportation machine to the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)

positions.summary: Says he is working to reverse Medicaid cuts and to keep health care tax credits from expiring, and criticized the government shutdown over extending health care assistance.
positions.quote: Congressman Amo shared how he’s fighting to reverse Medicaid cuts and to ensure Republicans don’t let health care tax credits expire.

positions.summary: In June 2025 said only Congress can declare war and joined a bipartisan House coalition seeking to enforce the War Powers Act after U.S. strikes on Iran.
positions.quote: Our Constitution says that only Congress has the authority to declare war. Presidents do not get a blank check to engage in endless foreign conflicts.

positions.summary: In April 2025 criticized the Trump administration's trade war and pledged to protect Rhode Islanders from what he called unnecessary tariffs that raise the cost of energy, groceries and gas.
positions.quote: I’ll continue to fight to protect them from harmful cuts and unnecessary tariffs.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 Congress, serves on the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, the House Committee on the Budget, and the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

candidates.name: Kellie Keenan

summary.text: Kellie Keenan is the Republican nominee for Rhode Island's 1st District. In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey she describes herself as a public health professional, small business owner, wife and mother of three daughters with more than a decade of experience in healthcare and community programs. She is running on infrastructure and permitting reform, community health centers, and housing and energy affordability.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Boston Latin School and an advanced certificate in public health management from Suffolk University.
Describes herself as a lifelong New Englander and has worked more than a decade in healthcare and community health operations, including with Community Health Centers and federally funded programs.
Ballotpedia lists her career experience as public administration.
Describes herself as a wife, mother of three daughters, and small business owner who is not a career politician.
Advanced from the September 9, 2026 Republican primary for the 1st District, in which she was the only candidate on the ballot.

priorities.text: Infrastructure modernization and permitting reform, saying government red tape drives up costs and delays projects.
Strengthening Community Health Centers and expanding access to primary care and the healthcare workforce.
Lowering energy and housing costs through an "all-of-the-above" energy strategy and expanded housing development, particularly starter homes and small multifamily housing.

statements.quote: I will support an all-of-the-above energy strategy that includes reliable domestic energy production, nuclear energy, natural gas, and emerging technologies to improve energy security and reduce costs.
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, June 18, 2026

statements.quote: In Congress, I will advocate for policies that strengthen Community Health Centers, expand the healthcare workforce, reduce unnecessary bureaucracy, and improve access to affordable, high-quality care.
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, June 18, 2026

statements.quote: I will also advocate for permitting reform, reducing unnecessary regulations, and expanding housing development—particularly starter homes and small multifamily housing
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, June 18, 2026

candidates.researchNotes: Statements taken from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; her campaign website could not be loaded. No statements found on most other guide issues.

candidates.name: Pedro Soares de Souza

summary.text: Pedro Soares de Souza is an independent candidate for Rhode Island's 1st District; his campaign website presents his name as Pedro DeSouza. It describes him as someone who has worked in restaurants, built a small business and moved into a data career, and lists affordability, housing, single-payer health care and ending foreign wars among his positions.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is not a career politician: he has worked in restaurants, built a small business, and worked his way into a data career after COVID.
Ballotpedia lists him as an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 ballot for Rhode Island's 1st District.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, or other public statements found for Pedro Soares de Souza beyond his listing as an independent general-election candidate.
